To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the betaLCRs are able to reproducibily and stably express the HBB gene at full physiological levels and that low levels of transcription can support efficient episomal replication.
the beta-globin LCR-HBB gene cassette is able to express at full physiological and tissue-specific levels when inserted into a plasmid vector that includes the human IFNB1 S MAR element.

a beta-globin promoter and locus control region can be used to express a human beta-globin gene from within the context of an S/MAR element based episomal vector at levels that are equivalent to those found in the endogenous gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel replicating episomal vector (REV) technologies that can be used in a variety of gene transfer applications.
the development of a new type of replicating episomal vector (REV) for gene therapy and gene delivery applications.
the development of a generic and flexible replicating vector (REV) system based on the use of the IFNB1-S/MAR element.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S/MAR elements are able to confer a stable replication and retention function to episomal vectors in a manner that allows the expression of a wide range of transgenes.
the S/MAR is able to confer a stable and long-term episomal replication and expression function to a REV when stably transfeced and selected in mammlian cells.
a S/MAR element is a useful and flexible tool to provide stable expression of transgenes from an episomal vector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S/MAR-based REVS can provide long-term, physiological levels of transgene expression in an episomal state.
the S/MAR is a powerful and versatile element for episomal vector design and that it can be used to achieve high levels of tissue-specific expression from a single copy of a REV.
S/MAR element based replicating episomal vector systems are capable of providing long-term transgene function in the absence of selection in the target cell population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S/MAR-based REV system is able to provide stable and physiological levels of gene expression in a tissue-specific manner.
the betaLCRs can function to provide high levels of expression from a replicating episome.
the beta-globin gene locus control region can function to drive high-level expression from an episomal vector in a tissue-specific manner.
